fixes.explanation: Verse 2 says it plainly: “…the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah…” Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is the one who came to Jerusalem and besieged it (Daniel 1:1). Still, the text names the Lord as the One who delivered. It's a heavy verse, friend, so I'm not going to joke over it.

Laws are a reasonable guess for a palace job, friend. But verse 4 says Ashpenaz is to teach them “…the language and literature of the Chaldeans.” Laws never make the list. Ask me to bake a cake from a cookie recipe and I'd give you the same look. The blank is waiting on a different word.

History sounds like a smart subject, friend. But verse 4 says the teaching is “…the language and literature of the Chaldeans.” History never gets a seat in that line. Pick it for the blank and the verse just politely slides it back across the counter.

Robes are a fun guess, friend, but this passage never mentions them. Verse 7 says the chief official gave them names: Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. Nobody in that verse is getting measured for anything. I'd say the new robes are only in your imagination, and that's a good spot for them.

That one is true, and the chief official says it himself. He tells Daniel, “You would endanger my head before the king!” So he does name his own head as the thing at risk. That's a serious thing to say, friend.

Daniel asks, “Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.” That's the whole menu he puts on the table, and he asks for just ten days of it. Picture that request landing at a king's table, friend. I'd have asked for a cookie on the side.

Close on the water, friend. Verse 12 has Daniel asking, “Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.” Bread didn't make the cut. Vegetables are the food on his list, and for a ten-day test that's one short menu.

Fruit and milk make a fun menu, friend, but it isn't Daniel's. In verse 12 he asks, “Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.” Vegetables and water, and that's the order. Short menu, big test.

Right, they don't look thinner. Verse 15 says “…they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.” That's the opposite of what the chief official feared in verse 10. I bet that surprised somebody.

Verse 16 says “…the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.” The test ended and the vegetables kept coming. When something works, friend, you don't touch it. I'd do the same with my best cookie recipe.

That's not what the steward does. Verse 16 says he “…continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.” The four of them stay on vegetables. The royal food doesn't come back for them.

Verse 19 says the king spoke with them, “…and among all the young men he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.” Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, looked at the whole group and found no one equal to these four. Then they entered the king's service. Three years of training, and these four came out on top.
